n1.text: Space is silent. With no air to carry it, even a scream dies at the lips.

n2.text: Past the Moon, where the pull of Earth and the pull of the Moon balance out, a single keeper tends the relay.

n3.text: On day four hundred, a ship came falling inward, at eight tenths of the speed of light.

n4.text: At that speed, space itself shortens along the line of motion. The ship arrives squeezed to three fifths of its length, and its light is pushed toward blue.

n5.text: Its clocks run slow. While the keeper waited five years, the traveler aged three.

n6.text: And light takes time to travel. The ship he saw was already a memory. By the time its image arrived, the traveler was here.

a1.text: Keeper. You hold the other half of my blade.

n7.text: Two blades, forged as an entangled pair. Two halves of a single quantum state.

a2.text: Return it. Or fight for it.

n8.text: One more thing. What you are about to hear is not sound crossing space. It is vibration, carried through steel, glove, and bone.

n9.text: Every push is shared. When the blades meet, both fighters fly apart, equal and opposite. Momentum is conserved.

n10.text: The keeper pulls his limbs in. Same angular momentum, smaller body. He spins faster.

n11.text: The alien's blade is not in one place. It is a cloud of maybes, until something touches it.

n12.text: He raises a barrier. Most of the wave reflects. But a quantum wave never fully stops. A sliver tunnels through.

n13.text: Then the keeper measures his own blade.

n14.text: Spin up. And across the gap, with nothing crossing it, the other blade is spin down.

n15.text: No signal outran light. The answer was shared from the start. Entanglement carries no message. Only agreement.

n16.text: The traveler left, its light sliding into red. Three years home, by its own clock. Five, by ours.

n17.text: And the lost blade drifts on, in a straight line, forever. Nothing out here will ever stop it.
